hints: Notice the two black dots form a pair of common points, so the middle vertical branch with $4.1\text{ V}$ and $3.7\text{ V}$ is in parallel with the right-hand branch containing $2.2\text{ V}$, $1.2\text{ V}$ and R.
Recall Kirchhoff's second law for parallel branches: the total potential drop from the upper dot to the lower dot must be the same by either route.
Add the $4.1\text{ V}$ and $3.7\text{ V}$ drops to find the voltage between the dots, then set it equal to $2.2 + 1.2 + V_R$ and solve for $V_R$.
walkthrough: Identify the parallel section: the upper dot and lower dot are joined by two routes. One route is the two middle resistors in series, the other route is the $2.2\text{ V}$ resistor plus the $1.2\text{ V}$ resistor plus R in series.
Find the voltage between the dots using the middle branch. Resistors in series add: $V_{dots} = 4.1 + 3.7 = 7.8\text{ V}$.
Apply Kirchhoff's second law: the right-hand branch between the same two dots must drop by the same $7.8\text{ V}$.
Write the series sum for the right branch: $2.2 + 1.2 + V_R = 7.8$, where all values are in $\text{V}$.
Solve: $V_R = 7.8 - 3.4 = 4.4\text{ V}$. This is option A.

options.A: The right branch must have $7.8\text{ V}$ across it, so $V_R = 7.8 - 2.2 - 1.2 = 4.4\text{ V}$.
options.B: $4.6\text{ V}$ does not satisfy Kirchhoff's second law for the right-hand loop when added to $2.2\text{ V}$ and $1.2\text{ V}$.
options.C: $6.6\text{ V}$ results from an incorrect loop equation, such as adding instead of equating the two parallel branch voltages.
options.D: $11.2\text{ V}$ adds all five labelled voltages together, which ignores that the $4.1\text{ V}$ and $3.7\text{ V}$ resistors are in parallel with the branch containing R.
